IRREVERENTS — EXPANDED WORLD & GAME PROPOSALS

Navigation guide \| 22 November 2026

# A glimpse of the game

In an earnest kingdom where people care desperately about history, the heroes have been summoned to hear a solemn account of an imminent apocalypse. Their attention instead fixes on the king's stained-glass window, a champion's invincible-looking armor, the advisor's magic pills, a chained dragon and a suspiciously placed bookshelf. They might spend hours listening, leave politely, rob the vault, release the beast or throw the king through the window. Then they may find a hidden route from the palace basement into the city sewers, emerge in an ordinary marketplace, accidentally start a violent pursuit, commandeer a machine meant to stop them, escape into a ruined arena, and earn a memorial of the incident in a Hall they can subsequently rob.

That is the kind of PLAY the project intends to support. It is not the canonical story of what every player must do.

# World proposal in brief

A central capital with ceremonial spaces; an inhabited trade town; a multilayer forest; a reconfigurable waterworks; an industrial foundry; a crumbling arena with buried consequences; an elevated sky-route network; hidden underways joining apparently separate areas; a playable Hall of Legends; scattered sites tied to a world-threatening central crisis.

Every major region ought to offer ordinary peaceful use, an attainable stealth opportunity, a way to provoke escalating response, one or more compelling secrets, and meaningful reasons to return with later characters and powers.

The world should look and feel like a clean Amazing Mirror-era side-scroller at gameplay scale—not a visually overwhelming fantasy poster.

# The proposed first integrated slice

One playable throne room with public and hidden exits.

One narrow street with shops, a tempting high-security target and NPC traffic.

One undercroft with crawlspace, breakable wall, lever, alternative route and local recruit.

Two or three functional character types in a shared expedition party.

One temporary copied ability with stealth/combat/puzzle uses.

NPC suspicion, escalation, a heavy impact and one commandeerable security machine.

A safe escape route into a compact Hall gallery where a truly extraordinary event can be framed on a pedestal.

This is a scope suggestion, not an approved production commitment.

# How to evaluate these texts

Does the location invite “What would happen if I...?” rather than merely offer a quest waypoint?

Could the same room be approached silently or catastrophically with different outcomes?

Does the system work when the player ignores the expected order?

Are new discoveries likely to make players want to revisit earlier regions?

Can a multi-player feat become part of every participant's recorded history?

Is the central apocalypse actually important to the world but not forced into the player's priorities?

Do consequences produce additional interesting gameplay rather than harsh reset punishment?

If the answer is no, the proposal is not yet behaving like Irreverents.

# Next author decisions that would unlock detailed production plans

1. Decide how mythic, medieval, mechanical or modern the world can become. The current proposals mix fantasy with machines to support hijackable vehicles.

2. Select or reject a central crisis concept. “The Great Unbinding” is a candidate, not canon.

3. Set an initial playable party size and rough online player cap. Current docs deliberately leave this open.

4. Agree on the first two or three functional character types and first copied power.

5. Choose what kinds of destruction should persist, how heat cools, and how ordinary defeat recovers.

6. Approve one coherent game-scale pixel art direction, specifically reduced overstimulation.

These are not prerequisites for brainstorming more. They become important before engineering locks down systems.

# Editorial rule

Promote a world, name, faction, ability or narrative outcome from PROPOSED to CONFIRMED only after explicit owner agreement. Preserve rejected alternatives and avoid silently importing AI-generated art labels as narrative canon.

CORE PREMISE OVERRIDE — 22 NOV 2026

The owner has sharpened the world’s premise since this proposal bundle was written: people have made the Hero’s Journey a near-religious mandate. Everything and everyone must fulfill their exact, predictable sacred narrative role. The world takes its magnificent main quest seriously and finds even mundane objects intensely meaningful. The protagonists discover alternative uses, which inhabitants often find horrifying. Apply this to ALL proposed world, faction, crisis, encounter and character ideas; reject any earlier proposals that make the society broadly flexible, self-aware or quick to embrace subversion. Canonical new direction: https://docs.google.com/document/d/16hzOOStE4Nt-uOcD6ApTDbWPT10fgizTC3eOcDB8Vmw/edit

MAJOR TONAL OVERRIDE — DELIGHTED ROLE-PLAYERS (22 NOV 2026)

Update all proposals: the inhabitants of this intensely scripted, sacred Hero’s Journey world LOVE fulfilling their exact archetypal roles. The storekeeper is sincerely delighted and proud to be a storekeeper; likewise champions, sages, rulers, guards and villains love fulfilling their expected narrative purposes. Do not frame the world as oppressed, cynical or yearning for liberation. Their sincerity and joy is precisely what makes the heroes' bizarre interventions disruptive. Detailed confirmed direction: https://docs.google.com/document/d/16hzOOStE4Nt-uOcD6ApTDbWPT10fgizTC3eOcDB8Vmw/edit
